disposition: All concrete findings from this independent lexer/core/statement/resource/span review were corrected or explicitly classified and covered by retained evidence. This is a bounded review, not proof of complete C conformance.
covered_areas: UTF-8 byte boundaries in malformed C, string/character prefixes and escape scanning, preprocessing-number longest match, invalid tokens and EOF
Lexing work accounting, token-buffer capacity accounting before allocation, terminal budget failures, recursive parser guards, AST depth and clone/drop behavior
Statement loops, dangling else, labels, control-flow scopes, typedef shadowing, scope cleanup after parse errors, bounded attribute lookahead
Typedef-versus-expression lookahead and declaration scope boundaries without speculative environment mutation
GNU attributes in original tag positions, removal of semantic text normalization, original-source operand and closing-delimiter spans
Frozen parser/checked/Builder outputs, exact non-span value comparisons, explicit correction-manifest matching, and measured output provenance

findings.finding: Eager tokenization allocated retained token capacity before applying the configured memory budget and scanned long trivia/literals before charging work.
findings.resolution: Charge source scanning up front and token work separately; check the geometric capacity against max_cache_bytes before reserve_exact. Synthetic EOF and terminal failure checks prevent a partial token prefix from becoming a successful parse.

findings.finding: Nested introspection and a long control-statement chain caused stack overflow in the initial handwritten parser at the previous permitted recursion limit.
findings.resolution: The default and hard maximum recursive rule depth are 512; the independent AST-depth limit remains 1024.

findings.finding: The old in-place attribute delimiter compaction and record-attribute reordering did not map moved bytes back to the original source; new token endpoints exposed omitted delimiters and incorrect operand locations.
findings.resolution: Parse GNU tag attributes directly and remove semantic attribute text rewriting. Written delimiter and operand regression tests pass. Five independent record-attribute cases retain identical semantic units while fixing original-source locations.

findings.finding: The old parser accepted 0x1e+1 as an addition, although preprocessing tokenization requires one invalid preprocessing number.
findings.resolution: The token lexer rejects the complete invalid number; GCC and Clang independently agree across the checked C modes.

findings.finding: Consumed-token endpoints omit trailing trivia previously included by the generated parser. Correct attribute source mapping also restores 19 missing closing delimiters in the real-project checked snapshots.
findings.resolution: All AST values/counts and checked non-range values stay exact. The comparator proves 1,670 direct-parser and 17,133 checked whitespace trims and permits only 19 individually source-pinned delimiter restorations. Exact span/checked-JSON equality remains false.

limitations: Native execution and performance evidence here are x86_64 Linux only; this review does not establish macOS, Windows, or other-target performance.
Finite regression, differential, native, and sanitizer cases cannot prove complete C conformance or absence of every resource exhaustion path.
max_cache_bytes bounds retained parser-token capacity, not total AST allocation or process RSS. Allocation counters measure cumulative requests; RSS includes output serialization outside the timer.

The AST representation/API is retained, but source-span endpoints and some diagnostics intentionally differ. Callers comparing exact source ranges or error text must account for those documented changes.
The shared VM does not control unrelated tenant activity, frequency, or memory bandwidth. Pair ranges are observed ranges, not confidence intervals.
